spans.s:
Cedi is the name of a people who, with their king kaśu, the caidya, are mentioned only in a Dānastuti (‘Praise of Gifts’), occurring at the end of one hymn of the Rigveda, where their generosity is celebrated as unsurpassed. They occur later in the Epic with the Matsyas, and lived in Bandela Khaṇḍa (Bundelkhand). In Vedic times they were probably situated in much the same locality.
Foot notes viii. 5, 37-39.
Lassen, Indische Alterthumskunde, 12, 688, n. 3; Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 129; Pargiter, Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society, 1908, 332; Oldenberg, Buddha, 402.
